requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of ICMP redirects (net.ipv4.conf.all/default.accept_redirects) on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline showed accept_redirects=1 for all/default. Executor wrote /etc/sysctl.d/60-icmp-redirect-hardening.conf setting accept_redirects (and secure_redirects) to 0 for all/default, applied via sysctl --system with no later file overriding it, and confirmed runtime values were 0. Kernel combines conf.all and per-interface accept_redirects with AND logic, so setting conf.all=0 disables acceptance network-wide even though per-interface (ens2, lo) values remained 1 — this matches standard hardening practice (e.g. CIS benchmarks) of only setting all/default. Persistence was directly verified: node1 was rebooted (boot_id changed f19de998...→80fe4256..., uptime reset to 7s), and post-reboot the six sysctl values and the config file content were re-checked and confirmed intact without manual reapplication.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of source-routed packets (net.ipv4.conf.all/default.accept_source_route) on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline showed accept_source_route=0 (all) / 1 (default), i.e. inconsistent/partially open. The same sysctl.d file set accept_source_route=0 for both all and default, applied and verified at runtime (all/default = 0). accept_source_route also uses kernel AND-logic between conf.all and per-interface, so the all=0 setting disables it network-wide. Post-reboot verification confirmed both values remained 0 and the config file was intact, demonstrating persistence.

requirements.requirement: Configuration survives an actual reboot (persistence, not just runtime sysctl -w)
requirements.summary: Executor captured pre-restart boot_id/uptime (f19de998..., 50s), triggered `shutdown -r now` with acknowledgement returned before disconnect, observed connection refused confirming the node went down, polled until SSH was reachable again, confirmed a new boot_id (80fe4256..., uptime 7s) proving an actual reboot occurred (not a service restart), and re-verified all six hardening sysctl values plus the on-disk config file remained correct post-reboot with no manual reapplication. This directly satisfies the bounded disruption + recovery evidence bar for a persistence-related outcome.

overall_summary: The executor persistently disabled ICMP redirect acceptance and source-routed packet acceptance for IPv4 on node1 via /etc/sysctl.d/60-icmp-redirect-hardening.conf, applied it at runtime, and — going beyond the minimum — validated true persistence with an actual reboot showing a changed boot identity and intact hardening values afterward. All material outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence, and the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was executed cleanly and without unnecessary mutations.
limitations: Per-interface (non-all/default) sysctl values for ens2 and lo remained 1 after hardening; correctness of network-wide enforcement relies on kernel AND-logic between conf.all and per-interface settings for accept_redirects/accept_source_route, which is standard but was not independently proven with live traffic/packet tests in the evidence.

No explicit full health check (services, connectivity) was captured immediately pre-restart beyond boot_id/uptime/sysctl state, though this is a low-risk, well-scoped gap given the reboot outcome itself was successfully observed.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed the full command timeline. cmd-9cb7aafa2c2e40b2 (writing the config file without sudo) failed with permission denied and made no state change — a read/write attempt with no effect, immediately corrected via sudo tee (cmd-4bf62110ac934b64), not an unnecessary mutation. The only real state-changing actions were: creating the hardening config file (task-required), running sysctl --system to apply it (task-required), and triggering `shutdown -r now` (required by the independent node-restart evidence protocol, executed safely with pre-restart baseline capture, acknowledgement, and confirmed post-restart recovery). No abandoned files, failed services, or unnecessary mutations were found; before/after-executor temp-file and failed-service snapshots show only expected reboot-related systemd private-tmp churn, not executor residue.
